title: The Indian Councils Act 1861
definition: A landmark British Parliamentary statute that transformed the executive-dominated governance of India into a consultative framework, initiating the policy of association of Indians with legislation and decentralizing legislative powers.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for understanding the evolution of the Indian legislature, constitutional decentralization, portfolio system origins, and the historical seeds of representative government under British rule.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of The Indian Councils Act 1861.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
